2026-09-24 (claude-advisor-guided bug-hunt pass, see docs/benchmarks.md Bugs #8/#9): found and fixed two real correctness bugs in this feature's own code, not hypothetical. (1) VkKeyScanW('
') returns VK_RETURN with the Ctrl bit set on a US layout (empirically confirmed via a direct P/Invoke, result 525), and the render-widget typing tier only masked in the shift bit -- any '

(2) Both per-character typing loops passed a CancellationToken to Task.Run, which only prevents the delegate from STARTING if already cancelled, not from continuing once running -- a cancelled/timed-out type_text call kept silently typing the whole remaining string. Fixed with a per-character ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested(), verified live against a real owned window (cancellation stops a ~16s call in under 3s). (3) Separately, UiaThread's caller-side timeout only failed that ONE call's Task -- the underlying STA COM call kept running forever, wedging the single dedicated thread and, with it, every other queued/future call against ANY target, with no recovery short of restarting DCU. Fixed with a watchdog that detects a currently-executing item running longer than its own configured timeout plus a 2s grace period and replaces that worker, carrying over queued work; only the single genuinely-stuck call stays stuck. This test was confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix code via a scoped git stash of only UiaThread.cs before being counted as a real fix. features.title: Planner/controller separation
evidence: New SubgoalStore (src/ShadowUse/Automation/SubgoalStore.cs): an explicit, typed unit of planner intent -- objective (immutable from Define onward), required_data (WorkflowValueStore names that must be set first), and an optional postcondition (same app/condition/text shape as wait_for). Deliberately layered ABOVE the existing execution surface: click/set_value/jev_act/browser_* dispatch exactly as before and never reference a subgoal_id at all, so 'keep planner intent separate from low-level execution details' (F23-R02) holds structurally, not by convention. New MCP tools define_subgoal/get_subgoal/check_subgoal_readiness/check_subgoal_postcondition/complete_subgoal/escalate_subgoal. F23-R01's 'give Jev only the current bounded decision and relevant context' required no new work -- jev_decide/jev_act already only ever receive one snapshot+goal, never a subgoal list, unchanged by this feature.

check_subgoal_postcondition reuses wait_for's own condition-check code (a near-zero timeout call, not a second condition-matching implementation) -- zero duplicated logic. complete_subgoal refuses when a configured postcondition is not CURRENTLY met (a genuine live re-check via the same path, not a blind assertion); a subgoal with no postcondition configured completes on the caller's own assertion.

F23-T02 (escalation never silently changes the original objective): Escalate marks the current record permanently Escalated and creates a NEW record ('{id}#r1', '#r2', ...) that copies Objective from the prior record -- there is no parameter on escalate_subgoal, anywhere, that can supply a different objective. required_data/postcondition MAY be revised on the new record (the actual point of replanning); Objective structurally cannot be.

Found and fixed a real pre-existing bug while proving this live: UiaService.FindByTextAsync crashed the whole DCU process with an unhandled NullReferenceException when IUIAutomationElement.CurrentName legitimately returns null for some element (a genuine COM interop edge case -- CurrentName can return null, not just throw, and the existing try/catch only guarded against throwing). Never triggered by any prior test in this suite because no earlier FindByTextAsync call happened to walk a live tree containing such an element; check_subgoal_postcondition's live re-check was simply the first caller to hit it. Fixed by treating a null CurrentName the same as 'no name' (skip), matching the existing catch-and-skip behavior for an outright throw.

SubgoalStoreTests.cs (13 pure unit tests, no live UIA): define/find round-trip; duplicate id and partial-postcondition rejected; readiness correctly reports missing-then-ready; escalate marks the original Escalated with its objective and required_data preserved (or explicitly revised) on the new record; escalating twice produces independently numbered revisions ('#r1#r1'); escalating an already-escalated subgoal and completing an already-completed one are both rejected; every operation on an unknown subgoal_id throws.

Live evidence (native_evolution_regression.py, real WindowStressFixture): a subgoal starts not-ready (missing required_data), becomes ready once set_workflow_value is called; TWO real set_value dispatches happen under that one subgoal with no further subgoal-management call between them (F23-T01); its postcondition (the always-present 'Fixture status' element -- wait_for's text_exists/element_exists conditions match an element's accessible NAME, not its dynamic VALUE, so this deliberately tests the postcondition mechanism rather than conflating the two UIA properties) is met and complete_subgoal succeeds; completing it again is refused; a second subgoal with a postcondition that can never be met refuses completion, then escalate_subgoal is called -- the revision carries the IDENTICAL objective while the original is left permanently Escalated (F23-T02); the revision's updated postcondition is then met and it completes -- PASSED.

Full verification: .NET Release 463/463 (--blame-crash, ~1m22s, all green -- was 450, +13, no test-count regression from the FindByTextAsync fix). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity), visual_grounding_regression.py, private_data_workflow_regression.py, api_gui_mixing_regression.py all PASS (all exercise FindByTextAsync-adjacent code paths; none regressed). features.title: Separate text/content generation
evidence: No live text-generation model key exists anywhere in this environment (same documented constraint as F27/F46/F47/F55), so DCU never makes a live generation call itself -- reframed honestly per F24-R01's own wording ('use a separately configured generator'): DCU's real job is caching/deduping an externally-supplied generated value, never generating prose itself, extending the project-wide 'Jev/DCU never generates, only judges/caches among already-resolved values' principle one more step.

New MCP tool resolve_field_text(context_key, exact_text?, generation_input?, generated_text?) wired to a new pure TextGenerationCache (keyed by (context_key, SHA-256-hash(generation_input))) AND to F27's existing ModelRoutingRegistry.Select(TextGenerator, ...) -- this is a genuine internal consumer of ModelRoutingRegistry, not just its own MCP tools, directly closing the 'island store' gap an Opus 5.5 advisor consult flagged this session for six process-lifetime stores (see docs/capability-status.json's integration_advisory_2026_09_24).
F24-R01/T01: exact_text always returns verbatim with used_generator:false, never touching the cache or ModelRoutingRegistry at all -- live-verified.

F24-R02/T02: unchanged generation_input for the same context_key is a cache hit (cache_hit:true, reuses the previously supplied generated_text, no fresh generation requested); a changed generation_input is a genuinely different cache key -- a miss requiring fresh generated_text, never a silent reuse of stale prose under new context -- both live-verified.

Honesty guard live-verified: a miss with no generated_text and no configured TextGenerator provider returns a structured refusal, never fabricated text. A miss with no generated_text but a provider explicitly configured via configure_model_provider ALSO refuses -- DCU reports the provider's presence but never invokes it live, proving the 'DCU never generates, only caches' boundary holds even when a provider IS registered.

TextGenerationCacheTests.cs (5 pure unit tests): same input is a cache hit; changed input is a distinct miss; different context_keys with the same input never collide; HashInput is deterministic and case-sensitive; Remember overwrites an existing entry for the same key.

Live evidence (native_evolution_regression.py, real WindowStressFixture): exact_text bypass, no-provider refusal, first-generation recording, cache-hit reuse, changed-input miss, and configured-but-uncalled-provider refusal all PASSED in one sequence.

features.title: Configurable models and controlled failover
evidence: Scope decision, honestly narrowed: this environment has no live model API key (TYPESAFE_API_KEY/JEV_API_KEY absent, same constraint documented against F46/F47/F55), so F27 cannot include a real provider network integration. Implemented the genuinely testable content instead: a pure capability-aware routing/failover/compatibility registry with zero network calls of its own -- the real provider request is left to a caller or a future live adapter; this registry only ever answers which configured provider, if any, may be used.

New ModelRoutingRegistry (src/ShadowUse/Automation/ModelRoutingRegistry.cs): independently configures providers per ModelRole (planner | text_generator | judge | perception, F27-R01), each with declared capabilities (structured output, modalities, data_destination local|cloud) and a REQUIRED pinned_model_id (F27-R02 -- a floating alias alone is rejected at configure time; an optional resolved_alias records what an alias actually resolved to, for provenance only). New MCP tools configure_model_provider/attach_compatibility_adapter/record_provider_failure/select_model_provider.

F27-T02 (a provider missing a required typed primitive cannot be substituted without an explicit validated compatibility adapter): Select() requires an EXACT capability match by default; a CompatibilityAdapter may bridge a gap only when explicitly attached to that specific provider AND it declares bridging that EXACT gap ('structured_output' or 'modality:<name>') -- an adapter declared for one gap never silently covers a different one.

F27-T01/R02 (simulated provider failure drives configured failover; local-only never falls back to cloud): RecordFailure marks a provider's failure timestamp; Select skips any provider still inside a 5-minute failure cooldown, so a real recorded failure provably reaches the next lower-priority configured candidate. local_only in RequiredCapabilities excludes every non-'local' data_destination candidate outright, even when it is the ONLY configured provider for that role -- never a fallback of last resort. RecordFailure/Select never touch WorkflowRunner/ExperienceStore/RunTimeline state at all, so 'the task continues from the same state' holds by construction, not by extra plumbing.

ModelRoutingRegistryTests.cs (14 pure unit tests, zero network/live dependency): rejects empty provider_id/missing pinned_model_id/invalid data_destination; picks lowest-priority among satisfying candidates; refuses a missing capability with no adapter; accepts it only via an explicitly attached matching adapter; an adapter for one gap does not bridge a different gap; local_only refuses a cloud-only provider even as the sole candidate; a recorded failure causes real failover to the next candidate; empty failure reason and unconfigured-provider lookups are rejected.

Live evidence (native_evolution_regression.py, real DCU MCP process, no UI/window dependency since this is pure config/routing): two real providers configured for role=judge, select_model_provider picks the priority-0 one; record_provider_failure on it, then select_model_provider again picks the configured fallback; a cloud-only perception provider configured alone is refused outright under local_only; a text_generator provider missing structured output is refused, then accepted (adapter_used:true) only after attach_compatibility_adapter declares bridging exactly that gap -- PASSED.
Full verification: .NET Release 450/450 (--blame-crash, ~1m7s, all green -- was 436, +14). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity) PASS. Python pytest 17/17.

features.title: Experience memory and loop recovery
evidence: F28-R02 only (no-progress/repeated-fingerprint detection): new LoopGuard (process-lifetime, per-(window_id, element_id/coords) scope) is wired into the native click and set_value tools. click records progressed=(effect != "none") using the same UIA-state-delta computation the tool already returns to the caller; set_value records progressed=(the post-write readback equals the requested value) and is skipped entirely (loop_guard:null) when the value cannot be read back at all (e.g. a password field blocked by UIA E_ACCESSDENIED), since that is genuinely unknown progress, not a no-progress signal. A configurable threshold (default 3) triggers should_stop:true with a plain-text diagnosis; any observed progress, or a different action fingerprint on the same target, immediately resets that scope's counter. This is purely diagnostic and additive (a new loop_guard response field) -- it never refuses to execute an action and is not a Jev/permission gate.

Unit coverage (LoopGuardTests.cs, 7 tests, no UIA needed): threshold-triggered should_stop, progress resetting the counter, independent per-scope tracking, a different action fingerprint on the same scope resetting the counter rather than inheriting the prior count, explicit Reset, and constructor validation.

Live evidence: tests/native_evolution_regression.py's login scenario clicks the fixture's own read-only 'Fixture status' label three times in a row after a real sign-in (a genuine no-progress action: UIA reports effect:"none" every time since the control has no Invoke pattern and no value changes) and asserts should_stop stays false on click 1-2 and becomes true with a non-empty diagnosis exactly on click 3, against the live WindowStressFixture -- PASSed (F28-T01: a control that never changes state gets a diagnosed no-progress result). tests/test_native_evolution_regression.py gained 3 new unit tests for the failure paths (never diagnoses, diagnoses too early, and the oracle unexpectedly registering a real effect).

Browser parity: the shared browser_click/browser_fill `Act` helper records progress as any observable change to a whole-page fingerprint (URL + every candidate's selector/enabled/visible/text, password candidates excluded from the text comparison) between before and after the action, scoped per (page_id, target selector) and fingerprinted per action (click, or fill keyed by a hash of the value) -- an additive loop_guard field on every browser_click/browser_fill response, same shape and same non-blocking guarantee as native. BrowserLoopGuardTests.cs (3, fake IBrowserEngine, no live browser) covers a genuinely no-op click diagnosing a cycle by the third repeat, a fill that changes the target's text every call never flagging should_stop, and two different candidates being tracked independently.

F28-R01 (this turn): new ExperienceStore (src/ShadowUse/Automation/ExperienceStore.cs), a process-lifetime store keyed by (adapter, target_identity, task_intent) -> {app_version, environment, an optional ActionResolutionRecipe (F31's shape, reused rather than duplicated), outcome, failure_category, recorded_at}. Outcome/failure_category are always caller-asserted, never inferred by DCU from an apparently-completed action -- matching F28-R02's 'never promote an unverified successful-looking run to reusable memory' for the memory half too. New native tools record_task_experience/recall_task_experience (ComputerUseTools.cs): app_version is auto-detected per call via Process.GetProcessById(pid).MainModule.FileVersionInfo.FileVersion, degrading to "unknown" (not throwing) when a process refuses MainModule access. New browser tools browser_record_task_experience/browser_recall_task_experience (BrowserUseTools.cs): app_version is caller-supplied (defaults to "unknown") since a web app exposes no automatic version signal DCU can read. recall_task_experience/browser_recall_task_experience compare the live app_version to the recorded one: on a match, a stored recipe (if any) is re-resolved live against a FRESH snapshot/observation exactly like resolve_cached_action/browser_resolve_cached_action (never a replayed id); on a mismatch, they return advisory:true and deliberately do NOT attempt to re-resolve anything -- the caller must revalidate targets and postconditions themselves before trusting it (F28-T02). record_task_experience/browser_record_task_experience reject outcome=success paired with a non-null failure_category as a contradictory call.

F28-T02 could not be exercised live: the native fixture's real file version cannot change between a record and recall call within one test run without rebuilding the binary, and a web page has no automatic version signal at all. Covered instead by ExperienceStoreTests.cs's Lookup_IsAdvisory_WhenLiveAppVersionDiffersFromRecorded (direct unit test of the store, matching the existing precedent of BrowserActionResolutionTests testing an F31 origin-change miss via a fake engine rather than a live browser navigation).

Live evidence for F28-R01's record/recall roundtrip: tests/native_evolution_regression.py's login scenario now also records a login_submit experience against the live WindowStressFixture, recalls it (found:true, advisory:false, outcome:success, and the stored username-field recipe live-re-resolves to a real element_id), confirms an unrecorded task_intent misses cleanly (found:false, reason:not_found), and confirms outcome=success + failure_category is rejected -- PASSed. tests/test_native_evolution_regression.py gained 4 new unit tests for the failure paths (missing app_version, recall unexpectedly not found, recall hit for an unrecorded intent, and a conflicting failure_category silently accepted).

ExperienceStoreTests.cs (8 tests, pure unit, no UIA/browser): not-found lookup, a matching-version hit, an advisory mismatch, key-dimension independence (task_intent and target_identity), overwrite-on-re-record, a distinct-key Count, and a stored recipe surviving the round trip.

features.title: Cached action resolution
evidence: New shared ActionResolutionCache (process-lifetime, keyed by adapter/adapter_version/target_identity/schema/task_intent per F31-R01) is used by both new native tools remember_action_resolution/resolve_cached_action (ComputerUseTools.cs) and new browser tools browser_remember_action_resolution/browser_resolve_cached_action (BrowserUseTools.cs). A cache entry stores only AutomationId/ControlType/Name (native) or Role/Name/Selector (browser) -- never a live element/candidate id and never a success claim.

F31-R02 (re-resolve on hit, invalidate on schema change) is enforced structurally, not by an extra invalidation pass: resolve_cached_action always takes a fresh snapshot/observation, recomputes the schema fingerprint (order-independent hash of every element's AutomationId+ControlType, or every candidate's Role+Selector) and target identity (native: process name; browser: page origin) before doing the cache lookup, so a schema or origin change is a different key rather than a stale hit. On a key hit, the recipe is still matched against the CURRENT snapshot's elements by exact AutomationId+ControlType+Name (native) or Role+Name (browser); zero or >1 matches invalidate the entry and return hit:false with reason not_found/ambiguous.

Unit coverage (no live UIA/browser needed): ActionResolutionCacheTests.cs (9 tests) covers Remember/TryGet/Invalidate lifecycle, task_intent and schema both being independent key dimensions, schema-hash order-independence and change-detection for both native and browser fingerprint functions. BrowserActionResolutionTests.cs (5 tests, fake IBrowserEngine, no live browser) covers a clean miss with nothing remembered, a hit returning a live re-resolved candidate_id (not the id captured at remember-time, since browser candidate ids are minted fresh per observation), a miss after a structural schema change (a field added to the page), and a miss after the page's origin changes even though an identical button still exists (F31-T02).

2026-09-24 follow-up (closes this feature's own 'no speed/latency benchmark comparing a cache hit against a fresh Jev-mediated resolution' gap, F28/F31 convergence): both jev_act (native, ComputerUseTools.cs) and browser_jev_act (BrowserUseTools.cs) gained an optional task_intent parameter. When supplied and a matching F31 recipe was previously remembered, the call skips the Jev network round-trip ENTIRELY -- resolve_cached_action runs, and on a hit the resolved target is dispatched directly (decision_source:'cache_hit_fast_path'), recording a real measured decision_ms (the live re-resolution cost) instead of a real Jev HTTP round-trip. A cache MISS falls through to the existing Jev decision path completely unchanged. A successful Jev-driven decision made WITH a task_intent auto-remembers its chosen target (via the existing remember_action_resolution/browser_remember_action_resolution methods, called directly -- no new resolution logic), so the very next call with the same task_intent takes the fast path: learn once via Jev, replay fast without Jev thereafter.

Found and fixed two real bugs while proving this live (both are the SAME root cause, once on each adapter): the cache-check probe itself calls ResolveCachedAction, which always takes a FRESH live snapshot/observation as part of re-resolving -- but the pre-probe snapshot/observation captured earlier in jev_act/browser_jev_act was then stale relative to that fresh one, so the SUBSEQUENT real Jev decision's freshness check would reject Jev's own answer as stale purely because the fast-path's OWN probe had advanced the revision/epoch, not because anything genuinely changed. Fixed by re-fetching the snapshot/observation after a cache miss before building the Jev request. Separately on the browser side: the auto-remember call was originally placed AFTER Act() dispatched, but Act's own settle-phase re-observation mints fresh candidate ids for the whole page (documented repeatedly elsewhere in this project), so the pre-dispatch candidate_id was already gone from session.Page.LastObservation by the time remember ran, and RememberActionResolution failed silently (its own error return value was not being checked) -- moved the remember call to before dispatch, using the observation Jev actually decided against.

New BrowserJevToolTests.cs tests (fake Jev HTTP handler, no live network): JevAct_WithTaskIntent_SecondCallTakesCacheHitFastPathWithoutCallingJevAgain proves the FIRST call with a task_intent decides via real Jev (handler.CallCount==1, decision_source:'jev') and the SECOND call with the SAME task_intent takes the fast path (decision_source:'cache_hit_fast_path') while handler.CallCount stays at 1 -- a genuine, directly-measured proof that Jev is never called a second time, not just that the response looks different. JevAct_UnknownTaskIntent_FallsThroughToNormalJevDecision proves an unremembered task_intent behaves identically to omitting it. Live: tests/native_evolution_regression.py._run_jev_act_cache_fast_path proves the native fast path works even with Jev fully unavailable (no TYPESAFE_API_KEY in this process) -- since the cache check runs BEFORE any Jev call, a hit dispatches successfully regardless of Jev's real availability (content-verified: the field's value actually changed), while a genuine cache miss still falls through to the normal (here: unavailable) Jev error path unchanged.

F32-R01's fifth node kind, this turn: bounded-loop node, added as a preprocessing expansion rather than real runtime loop machinery. New WorkflowLoopExpansion (WorkflowNonUiSteps.cs): a nodes_json entry with 'kind':'bounded_loop' plus exactly one of 'items' (string array) or 'count' (integer) plus a 'template' ({app,tool,args}) expands into 0..count ordinary WorkflowNodeSpec entries ('{id}#0','{id}#1',...) inside create_workflow itself, BEFORE _workflows.Create is ever called. Every string value inside the template's args is recursively substituted for the literal tokens '{{loop_index}}' (always) and '{{loop_item}}' (items-loops only) -- objects/arrays nested inside args are walked, not just top-level fields. Generated nodes share the loop node's own prerequisites (parallel siblings by default, matching WorkflowRunner's existing wave scheduler); a caller needing sequential iterations chains '{id}#{index-1}' as an explicit prerequisite of a later node instead of a sixth mechanism.

RECORDED 2026-09-24 (bug-hunt round 2, undecided by design, not a code gap): http_request's allowed_hosts and read_file/write_file's allowed_root -- plus WorkflowValueStore.Resolve's value_env -- are parameters supplied by the SAME MCP caller the check restricts, not read from any operator-controlled Settings allowlist; the redirect-hop/path-traversal validation against that caller-supplied list is real and tested (F32-T02), but a compromised or prompt-injected caller can set the list to approve its own exfiltration target in the same call. This is a genuine property of the current design, verified against source, not a fabricated concern -- but closing it (adding an operator-level Settings allowlist the caller's own list must additionally satisfy) is a real change to DCU's trust model that conflicts on its face with the objective's own 'must not become a permission/security gate' principle, so it was deliberately left as a recorded, user-decidable finding rather than built speculatively. See docs/benchmarks.md's 'Round 2' section for full detail.

features.title: Parallel independent workers
evidence: F35-R01/T01 (resource leases; concurrency only when declared resources do not conflict; same-target requests serialise): new ResourceLeaseRegistry (src/ShadowUse/Automation/ResourceLeaseRegistry.cs) -- a process-lifetime per-resource-key SemaphoreSlim(1,1) table. Wired into WorkflowRunner's DAG-node dispatch path only (ComputerUseTools.DispatchWorkflowNode/WorkflowResourceKey): before dispatching a node, a resource key is derived -- native: app-selector plus element_id when the step names one (falls back to the whole app for wait_for/drag/scroll-without-target); browser: session_id plus candidate_id when named. Two nodes in the SAME concurrent wave (WorkflowRunner.RunAsync's Task.WhenAll) targeting the identical element/candidate now genuinely serialise instead of racing; nodes on different targets, including different apps and different browser sessions, never block each other. This specifically closes a real pre-F35 gap: native mutations were already always fully serialised process-wide by ComputerUseTools' pre-existing static _mutationLock (safe but coarser than a per-target lease), but browser DAG-node mutations had NO serialisation at all before this change.

F35-T02 (worker cancellation/crash releases/reconciles leases without letting an expired lease continue): DispatchWorkflowNode acquires the lease, then wraps the dispatch call in try/finally so DisposeAsync always runs, whether dispatch returns normally, throws, or is cancelled -- a lease is never left held by a node whose dispatch was interrupted. Lease.DisposeAsync itself guards against double-release with Interlocked.Exchange (a caller calling it twice, or a future caller pattern doing so accidentally, cannot over-release the semaphore and let two holders in at once).

ResourceLeaseRegistryTests.cs (5 tests, pure unit, real Task-pool concurrency -- not simulated ordering): AcquireAsync_SameKey_SerializesRealConcurrentHolders (8 real concurrent tasks racing the same key, a shared counter proven to never exceed 1 concurrently-held instance), AcquireAsync_DifferentKeys_NeverBlockEachOther (two different-key holders proven to be inside their held window SIMULTANEOUSLY via the same shared-gate technique WorkflowRunnerTests uses -- would deadlock/time out under any accidental cross-key serialisation), AcquireAsync_ReleasedLease_UnblocksTheNextWaiterOnTheSameKey, AcquireAsync_CancelledWhileWaiting_NeverLeaksThePermit (a cancelled waiter never holds, so a fresh acquire on the same key succeeds immediately afterward), DisposeAsync_CalledTwice_ReleasesOnlyOnce (proves the double-release guard by re-running the same real-concurrency proof immediately after a double-dispose).

Live regression: tests/native_evolution_regression.py's existing _run_dag_workflow (two independent native set_value nodes on DIFFERENT elements of the same window) and the new _run_mixed_dag_workflow (a native node feeding a browser node via a real prerequisite edge) both continue to PASS with the lease wired into every DAG dispatch -- proving the new mutual-exclusion layer does not deadlock or serialise genuinely-independent real nodes in production. No dedicated live scenario forces two DAG nodes onto the literal SAME element/candidate concurrently yet (see remaining_work) -- the SAME-target serialisation guarantee itself is proven only by the pure-unit tests above, not by a live fixture.

Full suite after this feature: .NET Release 323/324 (--blame-crash, ~10-16m across reruns; the 1 failure, LiveInstalledEdge_ConditionWaits_HandleDebouncePollingNavigationAndTimeout, is unrelated browser condition-wait code this session never touched -- failed 3x in immediate back-to-back isolated reruns during a period of heavy back-to-back dotnet-test/Edge-process load from this same session, then passed cleanly after a short idle period, consistent with resource-contention flakiness rather than a regression). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity, including the mixed-adapter DAG) PASS. Python pytest 17/17.

evidence: F42-R01 (expose what each target currently supports) was already real on the native side and undercredited: ElementInfo.SupportedOperations (UiaService.cs) reports click/set_value/scroll per element from actual UIA pattern availability (Value/Toggle/Scroll patterns), surfaced in get_app_state as supported_operations and consumed by BuildNativeJevRequest to filter candidates before any Jev call.

New BrowserCapabilities.SupportedOperationsFor(role, type) (src/ShadowUse.Browser/BrowserCapabilities.cs) derives real per-candidate operations from the actual HTML tag/type captured at observation time -- click-only for button/a, fill+click for text-like input/textarea, click-only for select (Playwright.FillAsync rejects <select>, so claiming fill there would be a false capability the caller would then watch fail), click-only for checkbox/radio/submit/button/reset/image inputs, and upload-only for file inputs. Wired into ObservedElement/BrowserCandidate and now returned as supported_operations on every browser_open/browser_observe/browser_wait candidate (F42 spec example in SPEC_DCU_JEV_EVOLUTION.md shows exactly this shape).

Found and fixed a real pre-existing accuracy bug while building this: BrowserUseTools.InferOperations (used only for filtering Jev candidates, a narrower and separately-tuned question) claimed every input/textarea/select was fillable regardless of type -- wrongly telling Jev that checkbox/radio/file inputs and <select> elements supported fill. Left InferOperations itself unchanged (switching it to the new accurate SupportedOperations would have deregistered every existing test fixtures candidates from the Jev action space, since fixtures do not set the new field) but documented the divergence in a code comment so it is not mistaken for redundant duplication.

Architecture pivot (Opus 5.5 advisor consult, CLI fallback, before implementing the coordinate-bridge fallback -- a major architectural decision per the objective's own guidance): the advisor reviewed the native-HWND bridge design (PostMessage clicks at a screen point translated from a Playwright bounding box) and recommended AGAINST it. Reasoning, confirmed against this codebase: (1) the browser chrome offset (address bar/tab height) is not queryable from Playwright and varies by browser build/app-mode/OS theme -- any calibration constant breaks silently on a browser update; (2) PostMessage into Chromium's Aura input handling (Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND) is itself a second, independently shaky mechanism on top of the coordinate mapping; (3) it cannot work headless at all, since BrowserHostWindow correctly returns null there; (4) CDP's own Input.dispatchMouseEvent (via Playwright's page.Mouse) already dispatches genuinely isTrusted events directly in Chromium's own viewport coordinate space -- no OS cursor movement, no chrome-offset math, and it works headless -- so it strictly dominates the native-HWND path for every case the native bridge could have reached. Adopted instead: a same-process CDP/Playwright point-click fallback gated by a structural verification probe (a one-shot capture-phase pointermove/pointerdown listener records the browser's OWN resolved event target and coordinates BEFORE any press is sent) so a wrong click is structurally impossible, not merely unlikely -- a probe mismatch aborts with zero presses, every time.

Implemented: BrowserPointClickResult (BrowserContracts.cs); IControlledPage.PointClickAsync (IBrowserEngine.cs) with a real implementation in PlaywrightBrowserEngine.cs -- fresh BoundingBoxAsync at click time (never the stale observation-time box), a static document.elementFromPoint pre-check, then the live pointermove/pointerdown probe around page.Mouse.MoveAsync/DownAsync/UpAsync, canvas targets marked 'point-verified' (only the dispatch point is provable) vs 'element-verified' otherwise. Deliberately scoped to the main frame only (BoundingBoxAsync is main-frame-relative but a sub-frame's own elementFromPoint needs frame-local coordinates -- an unbuilt translation, not guessed) -- throws BrowserUnsupportedException for any other frameId. BrowserPageSession.CheckClickReadinessAsync (exposes the existing UIA-readiness-style structural pre-check without dispatching, so route_click decides the same way the native branch already does via SupportedOperations, never by parsing an exception message) and BrowserPageSession.PointClickAsync wire it through BrowserSessionManager. evidence: F43-R01 (stop/cancel, per-operation timeouts, run step limits): every MCP tool method accepts a CancellationToken threaded from the MCP protocols own cancellation, so an operator/caller can stop a hung call immediately without a DCU-specific abort mechanism. JevClient enforces a per-call timeout (JevOptions.TimeoutMs) with bounded exponential-backoff retry on 429/503/529 (JevControllerTests.RateLimited_RetriesThenSucceeds, ServerError_ExhaustsRetriesThenThrowsUnavailable -- MaxRetries=0 proves it does not retry forever). browser_wait/BrowserSessionManager.WaitAsync enforces an explicit timeout_ms per call and returns unknown/TimedOut=true rather than hanging (BrowserAdapterContractTests.BrowserWait_ReturnsUnknownOnTimeoutAndAcceptsTypedPredicate, LiveInstalledEdge_ConditionWaits_HandleDebouncePollingNavigationAndTimeout against a live browser).

F43-T01 (a hung test provider cannot block the controller forever; the operator can stop immediately): demonstrated for the Jev HTTP path (TimeoutMs-bounded, retries exhaust and throw rather than hang) and the browser wait path (TimedOut result within the requested timeout_ms) -- both verified by the tests above. No run step limit (a cap on total actions per task) exists.

features.title: Browser network and console diagnostics
evidence: New browser_diagnostics MCP tool returns the sessions recent console errors, uncaught page exceptions, and failed/error-status (>=400) network requests. features.title: Performance and environment profiling
evidence: F51-R01 (measure observation, decision, dispatch and settling time separately, plus full task wall time): RunTimelineEvent (F48) gained optional DecisionMs/DispatchMs/SettleMs fields alongside the existing total DurationMs. Browser: the shared Act helper (used by browser_click/browser_fill/browser_jev_act) now times the actual action(...) dispatch call and the post-action ObserveAsync settle call as two separate Stopwatch checkpoints, and accepts an optional decisionMs passed through from browser_jev_act (Jevs own decision.LatencyMs) -- every response now carries a timing:{decision_ms,dispatch_ms,settle_ms,total_ms} object, not just a lump total. Native: click gained the same dispatch/settle split (the ClickElementAsync/ClickAtAsync call vs the post-action snapshot refresh) and a timing object on its response; jev_act records a separate jev_decide timeline entry (DecisionMs=decision.LatencyMs) immediately before delegating to click/set_value, so a caller reconstructing a fast-loop step pairs the jev_decide entry with the click/set_value entry that follows it.

The three phases are additive and best-effort by design (documented on the record): they will not always sum exactly to the total, since surrounding bookkeeping (validation, locking, the fixed post-action settle delay) is real time that is not attributed to any single phase -- this was confirmed, not just assumed, by live evidence below (dispatch_ms=106 + settle_ms=307 versus total_ms=685 for the same live click).

BrowserJevToolTests.cs: JevAct_ExecutesTheChosenClick now asserts result.timing.decision_ms equals the top-level latency_ms (proving the two are the same real measured value, not independently faked) and that dispatch_ms/settle_ms/total_ms are all non-negative; Click_RecordsToTheRunTimelineWhenEnabled now also asserts a plain (non-Jev) clicks timeline entry has DecisionMs:null but real DispatchMs/SettleMs, and that the response echoes the same via timing.decision_ms being JSON null -- proving the breakdown is not Jev-exclusive.

Live evidence: native_evolution_regression.py._run_timing_breakdown clicks the live WindowStressFixture and asserts the response carries a real, non-negative dispatch_ms/settle_ms/total_ms breakdown -- PASSED (observed dispatch_ms=106, settle_ms=307, total_ms=685 in one run; values vary run to run as expected for a real measurement, not a fixed number).

F51-R02 (controlled browser CPU/network/viewport conditions for repeatable performance tests) is entirely unimplemented -- no CDP emulation/throttling hooks exist. F51-T01 (a benchmark report can identify whether Jev, observation, or settling dominates) is satisfiable by a caller reading the new timing field per action, but no aggregate benchmark-report tool exists yet that summarizes this across a run (that is F53s job, still planned). F51-T02 (slow-network tests show adaptive waits rather than fixed delays) is unaddressed by this slice -- browser_wait already polls rather than sleeping a fixed amount, but that was pre-existing (F17/F45 era) and not newly verified here.
Full suite after this change: .NET 311/311 (Release, --blame-crash, ~10m23s, all green). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity) PASS. Python unittest across tests/test_*.py: 17/17.

2026-09-24 follow-up (extends the breakdown everywhere it was missing, closes most of this feature's own remaining_work): set_value gained the same dispatch/settle split as click (a timing field on its response, a DispatchMs/SettleMs-populated timeline entry). press_key/scroll/drag (native, previously recorded NO timeline entry at all) and browser_download/browser_upload/browser_dialog (browser, same gap) now record a single-phase dispatch_ms/settle_ms(=0)/total_ms breakdown and a RunTimelineEvent each -- honest about having no settle/re-observation phase of their own, not a fabricated split.

New get_benchmark_report MCP tool (ComputerUseTools.cs) plus a pure RunTimelineBenchmark.Summarize (src/ShadowUse/Automation/RunTimelineBenchmark.cs, no live tool dependency) close F53/F51-T01's aggregate-report gap: groups recorded run-timeline entries by (surface, action, jev_driven -- true only when a real DecisionMs was recorded, never inferred from the action name), reporting count/ok_count/avg-min-max total_ms, avg decision/dispatch/settle_ms, and which phase dominated. Grouping jev-driven and non-jev calls of the SAME action separately makes a jev=off vs jev-assist/fast-loop comparison for that action a direct read of two groups, matching the objective's own explicit benchmarking priority.

Found and fixed a real, pre-existing, wide-reaching bug while proving get_benchmark_report live for the first time (no prior session had actually turned EnableRunTimeline on end-to-end -- only the per-action timing FIELD, which is independent of it, had been live-tested): Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData) on Windows resolves via the Known Folder API and does NOT honor a process-level APPDATA environment-variable override -- it always returns the real logged-on user's roaming profile folder. Every Python live regression that redirects APPDATA for test isolation (native_evolution_regression.py, visual_grounding_regression.py, and private_data_workflow_regression.py transitively) had therefore been silently loading/writing the REAL C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\shadow-use\settings.json this whole time, not an isolated per-test copy -- confirmed directly with a --doctor debug probe (APPDATA env correctly read as the redirected path, but GetFolderPath still returned the real roaming folder regardless). Fixed by adding ShadowSettings.ApplicationDataFolder() (reads the APPDATA env var directly, falling back to GetFolderPath only when genuinely unset) and using it for both the settings.json candidate path and RunTimelinePath's default. Verified the fix directly (same --doctor probe now resolves the redirected folder) and via full regression: native_evolution_regression.py --scenario all (login+ambiguity), private_data_workflow_regression.py, and visual_grounding_regression.py all rerun clean under now-genuinely-isolated settings; no test's expected values happened to depend on the previously-real (unintentionally shared) settings file.

New tests/ShadowUse.Tests/RunTimelineBenchmarkTests.cs (5 pure unit tests, no file I/O): groups by surface/action/jev-driven, identifies the dominant phase by summed phase time (not just averages), reports 'unattributed' honestly when no phase breakdown exists at all, counts failures separately from successes, and handles empty input. New live native_evolution_regression.py._run_benchmark_report (EnableRunTimeline now turned on for the whole login/ambiguity scenario run via _settings_environment): exercises press_key/scroll (asserting their new timing field), then calls get_benchmark_report and asserts enabled:true, at least one group, native click/set_value/press_key/scroll groups all present, and every non-empty group has a dominant phase and a non-negative avg total -- PASSED. Incidentally revealed a genuine, correct (not a bug) insight from the tool itself: click's dominant phase is 'unattributed', because the 140ms cursor-pulse visibility delay between validation and dispatch is real elapsed time not attributed to either the dispatch or settle phase -- exactly the kind of finding F53 is meant to surface.

Full suite after this session: .NET Release 329/329 (--blame-crash, ~4m13s, all green, no flake this run). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity) PASS under real settings isolation. private_data_workflow_regression.py and visual_grounding_regression.py both PASS. Python pytest 17/17.

features.title: Human takeover and resume
evidence: F54-R02/T02 (discard stale queued actions after takeover): WorkflowNodeStatus gained Cancelled. New WorkflowRunner.PauseForTakeover marks every currently Pending node Cancelled and returns the cancelled ids; already-Running or terminal nodes are left untouched (an in-flight action cannot be un-dispatched, a genuinely different case from F29-T02's interrupted-node handling). Structural, not a runtime skip: RunAsync's own ready-node query only ever selects Status==Pending, so a Cancelled node can never be dispatched by a later RunAsync call. New MCP tool pause_for_takeover. get_workflow_status's done field now also treats cancelled as terminal.

F54-R01/T01 (resume from what is actually on screen after a user edits a field during takeover): no new capture mechanism was needed -- get_app_state (without a continuation token) and capture_workflow_value already always take a FRESH live UIA snapshot rather than serving a cached pre-takeover value. The genuinely new part was proving this holds together with the cancellation half in one live scenario.

WorkflowRunnerTests.cs (3 new pure unit tests): a queued node is cancelled and its dispatch delegate is proven never invoked on a later RunAsync call; a Running node and an already-terminal node are left untouched by PauseForTakeover; pausing an unknown workflow throws.

Live evidence (native_evolution_regression.py, real WindowStressFixture): a create_workflow with one Pending set_value node targeting the live username field is paused via pause_for_takeover; a set_value call then simulates a user editing that same field during takeover to a fresh value; run_workflow is called again and reports done:true with the node still cancelled (the queued sentinel value never appears on the field); a subsequent snapshot reads exactly the user's live-edit value -- PASSED.

features.title: Intent-aware search and filtering
evidence: Scope decision, honestly narrowed: the spec's donor (Jev Instant Search/Sift/Launcher) implies indexing browser history/files/email plus optional semantic Jev reranking; this environment has no live model API key (same constraint already documented against F46/F47) and DCU has no browser-history API at all, so browser history and email are explicitly OUT of scope (never read by this or any tool) rather than half-built. Implemented the genuinely local, boundable, already-real source: a caller-rooted filesystem search (LocalFileSearch, src/ShadowUse/Automation/LocalSearchService.cs), which also happens to be the only source with real, distinct opened/modified/added timestamps needed to test F55-T02 honestly.

New MCP tool search_local_files: recursive filename substring search bounded to allowed_root (same containment shape as WorkflowFilePaths). Every candidate reports opened_at/modified_at/added_at as THREE SEPARATE fields (File.GetLastAccessTimeUtc/GetLastWriteTimeUtc/GetCreationTimeUtc) -- never collapsed into one ambiguous 'recency' field, so nothing can be silently substituted for anything else (F55-T02's structural half). sort_by picks which dimension ranks results; ApplySortAndFallback only falls back to modified_at, and only when the requested dimension is unavailable for EVERY candidate, always reporting sort_fallback_used/sort_fallback_reason explicitly (F55-T02's fallback-labeling half) -- a candidate simply missing one dimension while others have it is never treated as a fallback case, it just sorts last.

New SearchSequencer (F55-T01, 'late search responses do not overwrite a newer query'): a process-lifetime monotonic sequence counter per caller-chosen scope. Begin() at query start, IsFresh() checked at completion; stale:true means a strictly newer query for the same scope has already begun since this one started. Pure in-memory bookkeeping with zero live/Win32 dependency -- the staleness-under-overlap guarantee itself is proven deterministically by LocalSearchServiceTests (SearchSequencer_OlderQuery_IsStale_OnceANewerQueryBegan) rather than a timing-dependent live concurrency race, which would only add flakiness, not additional confidence, to logic that has no environment-specific behavior to prove live.

F55-R02 ('keep data local unless explicitly permitted'): holds by construction, not a runtime permission check -- search_local_files never calls Jev, never reads browser history, and never reads email; there is no model call anywhere in this code path to permit or deny.

LocalSearchServiceTests.cs (14 pure unit tests): sequencer freshness/staleness/cross-scope independence; sort-by-requested-dimension when available; a candidate simply lacking one dimension is never treated as a fallback case; fallback only triggers when EVERY candidate lacks the requested dimension, with the original requested kind still honestly reported; requesting modified_at itself never falls back; max_results bounds enforced; real filesystem enumeration (temp dir) filters by substring case-insensitively and reports real modified_at/added_at.

Live evidence (native_evolution_regression.py, real temp directory with real files): search_local_files with query='invoice' returns exactly the two matching files sorted newer-modified-first (one file's mtime forced an hour into the past via os.utime, proving genuine sort by real timestamps, not creation order); every candidate reports all three recency fields non-null; a second call with query='unrelated' returns only the non-matching-named file, proving the query genuinely scopes results; query_sequence increases monotonically across two real MCP calls in the same scope and neither reports stale (non-overlapping calls); a different scope starts its own sequence at 1, independent of the first; an unsupported sort_by is rejected before any filesystem work -- PASSED.
Full verification: .NET Release 436/436 (--blame-crash, ~1m36s, all green -- was 422, +14). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity) PASS. Python pytest 17/17.

New MCP tools: preview_grid_schema (F57-R01 heading-to-schema preview), record_grid_cell_edit (bumps a cell's edit_version on a direct user edit), resolve_grid_cell (cache lookup by content/rubric/model, then applies-or-rejects against the cell's edit_version, recording the pre-run value under batch_id), undo_grid_batch, keep_grid_batch.

features.title: Voice turn-taking and interruption
evidence: No speech-recognition pipeline exists anywhere in this environment (same documented no-live-external-service constraint as F24/F27/F46/F47/F55/F57) -- reframed honestly the same way as those features: DCU never runs speech recognition itself, it owns the deterministic turn-taking state machine around transcripts the caller's own adapter supplies (partial/final text tagged with a caller-assigned generation_id).

New pure VoiceTurnController (per-session Listening/Finalized/Stopped/Failed state, latest generation_id tracking, a declared-at-open fallback_behavior) plus 6 new MCP tools: open_voice_session, submit_voice_partial, submit_voice_final, check_voice_silence_timeout, stop_voice_session, report_voice_transcription_failure.

F58-T01 live-verified: a partial transcript never finalizes regardless of content or how long it sits, however many times submitted; a stale/out-of-order generation_id is rejected outright; check_voice_silence_timeout below its threshold defers (returns finalized:false, reason:below_silence_threshold) while crossing the SAME caller-chosen threshold finalizes the last partial -- proving the exact bound is test-driven, not a copied demo constant (F58-R02).

F58-T02 live-verified: an explicit submit_voice_final hands off through define_subgoal's EXACT SAME SubgoalStore.Define used for typed goals (F58-R01's 'same planner/controller path') -- the returned subgoal_id is verified as a real, readiness-checkable SubgoalStore record, not a bespoke voice-only object. stop_voice_session is terminal and distinct from a new request: a late-arriving submit_voice_final for the stopped session is refused (reason:session_is_stopped) while a brand-new session_id opened afterward is completely unaffected. report_voice_transcription_failure returns the fallback_behavior declared at open_voice_session time, never a hardcoded default, and also marks the session terminal so a late response after a reported failure is refused identically to an explicit stop.

VoiceTurnControllerTests.cs (11 pure unit tests): partial never finalizes; stale generation_id rejected; explicit final hands off to a real SubgoalStore record with the correct objective; silence below threshold defers; silence crossing threshold finalizes the last partial; stop cancels a late final; stop does not affect a brand new session; transcription failure returns the declared fallback (not a hardcoded one); a late final after a reported failure is refused; an empty final transcript is rejected; opening a duplicate session_id throws.

features.title: Catalogue-constrained interface composition

features.title: Shared human-and-agent review state
evidence: New ReviewRoomStore (src/ShadowUse/Automation/ReviewRoomStore.cs): a process-lifetime collaboration-provider -- named rooms with authenticated membership (a per-actor shared-secret token established at first join, honestly scoped since no real identity provider is available in this environment -- the same 'no live external auth/model' constraint documented against F27/F55), ordered annotations, presence, and a single execution lease per room. New MCP tools join_review_room/post_annotation/list_annotations/undo_annotation/acquire_execution_lease/release_execution_lease/submit_execution_command. Nothing here is persisted to disk (F60-R01's 'minimum necessary persisted data' -- the whole room is in-memory, process-lifetime only, same caveat as every other *Store in this project).

F60-T01 (two reviewers see consistent annotations; only the lease holder may submit): ListAnnotations returns the exact same list to every caller -- no per-actor filtering. TryAcquireLease succeeds only when unheld or already held by the caller (reentrant), never stolen from a different current holder. submit_execution_command requires BOTH authentication (matching join token) AND current lease-holder status, refusing an unauthenticated stranger and an authenticated-but-lease-less member identically to any other caller.

F60-R02/T02 (undo affects only collaborative state, never reverses a real action): UndoAnnotation is a pure soft-delete on the annotation list -- the type has zero references to WorkflowRunner/ExperienceStore/RunTimeline/DispatchStep anywhere in the file, so there is no code path by which undoing a comment could touch an already-executed action even accidentally. submit_execution_command itself dispatches through the EXACT SAME DispatchStep routing table create_workflow/invoke_helper/dispatch_composition_action already use -- collaboration state is a gate in front of normal execution, never a reimplementation of it.

ReviewRoomStoreTests.cs (16 pure unit tests, no live UIA): join/authenticate round-trip; wrong token and unknown actor both refused; re-joining with a different token is refused (impersonation protection) while the same token is idempotent; two reads of ListAnnotations after one post are identical; empty annotation text rejected; undo removes an annotation and a second undo on the same id returns false; lease acquisition succeeds when unheld, is reentrant for the holder, refuses a different actor, and can be released then re-acquired by someone else; GetOrCreate returns the same room instance for the same id.

Live evidence (native_evolution_regression.py, real WindowStressFixture): alice and bob both join a room; alice posts an annotation both reviewers read identically; a never-joined stranger and an authenticated-but-lease-less bob are both refused submit_execution_command; alice acquires the lease (bob's steal attempt fails); alice's submit_execution_command actually dispatches a real set_value, content-verified against the live username field; undo_annotation on alice's earlier annotation removes it from list_annotations while the real field value set by the earlier execution command remains completely unchanged -- PASSED.

Full verification: .NET Release 495/495 (--blame-crash, ~1m23s, all green -- was 479, +16, plus the same hardcoded app-selector-description-sweep regression every prior new-app-selector-tool session hits, fixed by wording on submit_execution_command). Both live native scenarios (login+ambiguity) PASS. Python pytest 17/17.
